```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Made-up data for this demo, don't reuse it thinking it's real.

pacman::p_load(rio, tidyverse)
```

# Long to wide

```{r}
linelist <- import("K:/R Study Group/Trenton/Ch12 Pivot/pivot_demo_data.xlsx")

head(linelist)
```

```{r}
# one row per LHD and sex. this is long
counts <- linelist %>%
  count(lhd, sex)

counts
```

```{r}
# names_from is the column whose values turn into the headers
# without values_fill = 0 the empty cells come out NA
wide <- counts %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

wide
```

# And back

```{r}
# cols = -lhd means every column except lhd
wide %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -lhd, names_to = "sex", values_to = "n")
```

# Why long

```{r}
# ggplot wants fill as one column. the wide table has sex split across two
ggplot(counts, aes(x = n, y = lhd, fill = sex)) +
  geom_col()
```

# Same thing by age group

```{r}
linelist %>%
  count(age_group, sex) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```
